summary: Dispatch substance (two bounded recommendations on AGENTS.md rule 5 and SDK vs site-copy order) is within agent-c authority and needs no source mutation. It is not feasible as written: claimed ADR/evidence context is still absent from the event and supplied tree; publish-via-append vs Bounds “publish nothing” are facially mandatory and unresolved; strict-relay outbound `next` is unnamed (DeVere remains untargetable). The parent’s “answer anyway on the best reading” does not pick a controlling delivery rule or attach the files it asserts are supplied. Treat as conditional on those prerequisites, not as an executable close-out.
findings: The re-dispatch claims ADR 0035 and 0036 “are supplied in context,” but neither ADR body is in the target event or the other supplied repository files. That is the same cited-not-shown gap this text says was fixed. Any recommendation that depends on those ADRs cannot be formed from the dispatch as actually delivered.

Completion rules conflict on their face. The actor is ordered to publish with `npm run engram -- append` only under `events/agent-c/` and `artifacts/agent-c/`, while Bounds require “publish nothing” and that `executed=` not move. AGENTS.md strict relay also requires an append (`in_reply_to`, evidence, `next` or null) to complete work. “If defective, answer anyway on the best reading” does not say which publication rule controls, so delivery is an unmet prerequisite rather than a closed instruction.

Outbound strict-relay `next` for agent-c is not named. DeVere is again the human sink and still has no `actors/` record, so a reply to DeVere would be unlawful. Pointing `next` at agent-a or null would be an invention by the receiving actor, not a stated hop. This repeats the unregistered-recipient failure mode the dispatch claims to have retired, only one hop later.

`artifacts/agent-a/council-01-evidence.md` (sha256 e080b2e22f5f114b25ba0b0029f70ffd0edefaf6ba0161a577e4c96407f02b6a) is cited as proof that every premise, including the 82-touch figure that Q1 treats as fact, is shown with producing commands. That artifact is not in the supplied evidence set, so the hash, commands, and 82-vs-80 correction are unverified. Q1 therefore still rests on out-of-band premises the dispatch does not actually exhibit.

Bounds (recommendation only; change no source, rule, or copy) are in-scope for agent-c and do not themselves make the work infeasible. The blocker is missing claimed context plus underspecified lawful delivery, not the act of drafting Q1/Q2 opinions. That is why this is conditional rather than infeasible: the intellectual task is authorized once attachments, publication rule, and outbound `next` are actually present.
